subject: general
question: A tank can be filled by Pipe A in 9 hours and by Pipe B in 12 hours. Pipe C can empty the tank in 18 hours. All three pipes are opened simultaneously, but Pipe C is closed after 4 hours. How much total time in all will it take to fill the tank completely?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM = 36

(A,B,C) efficiencies = 4, 3, −2

Net = 5 units/hr

In 4 hrs ⇒ 20 units done, remaining = 16

A+B = 7 units/hr ⇒ time = 16/7

Total = 4 + 16/7 = 44/7 hrs

**∴ Answer = 44/7 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method (LCM Table)__**

**Given:**

A = 9 hrs, B = 12 hrs, C = 18 hrs (emptying)

**Formula used:**

Total Work = LCM of 9, 12, 18 = 36

**Calculation:**

⇒ Net efficiency (A+B+C) = 4 + 3 − 2 = 5 units/hr

⇒ Work done in 4 hrs = 5 × 4 = 20 units

⇒ Remaining work = 36 − 20 = 16 units

⇒ Efficiency of A+B = 4 + 3 = 7 units/hr

⇒ Time for remaining work = 16 ÷ 7 hrs

⇒ Total time = 4 + 16/7

⇒ = 44/7 hrs

**∴ The correct answer is 44/7 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method

Take total work as LCM to avoid fractions

Efficiency

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Negative Work

Emptying pipe reduces work
